newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand sets power saving goal for 1997-2001.
newsitem.headline: Thailand sets power saving goal for 1997-2001.

text.p: Thailand will spend 19 billion baht ($760 million) during the next five years on energy conservation projects, said Piyasvati Amranand, head of the National Energy Policy (NEPO) on Monday.
The goal was to help save at least 1,000 megawatts of power annually, he said.
"This is a conservative figure. We hope the programme would enable us to save more as it goes along," he told reporters.
Thailand's daily energy consumption is equivalent to one million barrels per day of oil and the country footed an energy bill of around 200 billion baht ($8 billion) annually, he said.

"The demand is expected to rise by 10 percent every year. Since our indigenous sources are limited, we will rely more on procurement from abroad which will become more expensive in the future," he said.
Energy conservation schemes included technology development, studies for alternative sources of power, energy conservation legislation and campaigns to promote public awaremess.

According to data from the state-run Electricity Generating Authority of Thailand, the country's demand for electricity will grow to 13,009 mw by the end of this year, to 19,029 mw by 2001 and to 33,532 mw by 2001.
The country will need 253 billion baht during 1997-2001 to develop various power projects, EGAT data indicated.
Piyasvati said Thailand's natural gas will be depleted in 20 years unless new gas find is discovered.
Lignite reserves would probably last 30-40 years, he said. But the energy source was not popular because of negative impact on the environment.
"In the past, we focused more on expanding our procurement rather than conservation. It is about time to do it (conservation) seriously," he said.
"The biggest threat in the future is the cost of energy will be more expensive as our local sources are depleting. Conservation is one effective way to cut the size of the import bill," he said.
He said NEPO will also develop technology that will allow the country to be able to use more recyclable energy such as solar energy.
The multi-media nationwide campaign to promote public awareness of energy conservation is scheduled to start on Monday.
